title: Survey: 35% excluded from finance; women hold half of agent accounts
excerpt: A national survey finds 55.7% of women have no phone of their own. Bangladesh Bank data show women own about 13.8 million agent banking accounts.

image.alt: An ATM booth of a commercial bank in Bangladesh
image.credit: File photo: M.parvage / Wikimedia Commons, CC0

content:
About 35% of people in Bangladesh are excluded from formal financial services and 64.5% are included, according to the National Financial Inclusion Survey 2025 released in Dhaka on Wednesday (18 November), The Business Standard reported.

Separately, Bangladesh Bank's quarterly report shows women now hold about half of all agent banking accounts, The Daily Star reported.

The survey

More than half of women (55.7%) do not own a personal mobile phone. Only 8% of bank account holders use a debit card and only 21% of mobile financial service users use an app. About 34% of MFS users transact on basic phones costing Tk 1,000 to 1,200, and fewer than 4% use MFS for bill payments and other financial services.

About 70% of women and 59% of men do not know about spreading their investments to protect savings from inflation. Women receive remittances into bank accounts more often than men, 26.1% against 11.5%. M Abdur Razzaque of the research group RAPID gave the keynote at the launch.

Agent banking

At the end of September there were 27.8 million agent banking accounts, about 13.8 million of them held by women, and 85% in rural areas. Thirty banks run more than 20,600 outlets. Deposits rose 2.31% in the quarter to Tk 53,108 crore. The 2,244 women-owned outlets hold about 2.5 million accounts and Tk 4,822 crore in deposits.

Why it matters

For NGOs running savings groups, cash transfers or women's economic empowerment programmes, the phone gap matters most: digital payments do not reach women who have no phone. Agent banking is now a real rural channel that programmes can use.

What to watch

Whether Bangladesh Bank sets targets on women's phone and account access in its next financial inclusion strategy.
